questions.prompt: Which of these can be looped over twice and give the same items both times?
questions.explanation: range is a re-iterable sequence that creates a fresh iterator on every iter(). The other three are themselves iterators and are exhausted after one pass.

questions.prompt: A validator uses 'if v < lo or v > hi: raise ValueError'. What happens with v = float('nan')?
options: NaN is accepted only if lo is negative
NaN is accepted, because both comparisons are False
NaN is rejected, because it is not a number
TypeError is raised by the comparison
questions.explanation: Every ordered comparison with NaN is False, so neither branch fires. Writing 'if not (lo <= v <= hi)' rejects it.

questions.prompt: A plugin registry is filled by __init_subclass__. The config asks for 'lidar' but the registry is empty. Which cause is most likely?
options: The registry must be a metaclass attribute
The module defining the Lidar subclass was never imported
__init_subclass__ only runs for the first subclass
Class keyword arguments are not allowed
questions.explanation: The hook runs when the class statement executes. No import means no class statement means no registration.

questions.prompt: class R: p = property(lambda self: 1); def m(self): ... . After r = R(), which statement is true?
options: Both assignments work and shadow the class attributes on r
Both assignments raise AttributeError because the class owns them
r.m = 5 works and shadows the method; r.p = 5 raises AttributeError
r.m = 5 raises AttributeError; r.p = 5 works and shadows it
questions.explanation: Functions are non-data descriptors, so the instance dict wins after assignment. property is a data descriptor; without a setter, assignment raises AttributeError.

questions.prompt: A loader yields batches of 32 RGB images of 224x224 pixels stored as uint8 (3 channels). How many bytes of pixel data does one batch contain? Integer.
questions.skillLabel: Memory held by a lazy batch

questions.prompt: A running-sum sliding mean does 2 updates (one add, one subtract) for every sample after the first window is filled. With 1000 samples and window 100, how many such updates happen? Integer.
questions.explanation: Samples after the first 100: 900, each with 2 updates = 1800.

questions.prompt: batched(stream, 64) is applied to a finite stream of 1003 items. How many lists does it yield? Integer.
questions.explanation: ceil(1003/64) = 16: fifteen full batches (960 items) and one batch of 43.

questions.prompt: Base.__init_subclass__ increments a counter. A module defines X(Base), Y(Base), Z(X) and W(Z), and then creates 50 instances of W. What is the counter value? Integer.
questions.explanation: The hook runs per class definition (X, Y, Z, W = 4), not per instance.

questions.prompt: A pipeline does 'total = sum(data); peak = max(data)' where data = (read(f) for f in files). The sum is right but max raises ValueError. Explain why and give two fixes with their trade-offs.
rubric: Identifies that the generator expression is one-shot and exhausted by sum.
Fix 1: materialize with list() (simple, uses O(N) memory) or compute both in one pass.
Fix 2: wrap in a re-iterable (factory called per pass) at the cost of reading the files twice.
questions.explanation: Rubric-guided: compare your answer with each rubric point; this question is not automatically graded.

rubric: Prefers one reusable descriptor class to twelve copied properties (single validation rule).
Parameterizes lo and hi in __init__ and learns the name via __set_name__.
